ftp.cdc.gov now serves a certificate chaining to an Entrust root that current
CA bundles distrust, so the archives could not be fetched over a verifying
TLS chain. Integrity was established instead by content: the 2019 archive
extracts to a file byte-identical (sha256
2516b2b2ea679be52d012352deed74d00047f4fa2c0a8086872296cacbcd478b) to
data-raw/nhamcs/namcs2019, which has been committed to this repository since
2026-08-04. Re-verify that equality before trusting a re-download.

WHY THIS CSV EXISTS, AND WHY IT LIVES IN inst/extdata
This is the output of namcs_urps_payer_mix() -- an AGGREGATE of four payer
tiers, never microdata. The pooled .rds it derives from is ~2 MB and cannot
be committed (*.rds is .gitignore'd as a PHI/DUA control asserted by the
nightly leak-guard job), and data-raw/ is .Rbuildignore'd, so CI has no way
to reach the microdata. namcs_urps_payer_mix() falls back to this file when
the pooled .rds is absent, which keeps the 13 practice-economics and
end-to-end tests running against the real cited shares instead of erroring.

Reproduces three properties documented independently elsewhere in the repo:
  - Medicare:Medicaid within the government bucket = 92.3% : 7.7%
    (R/supply-practice_payer_mix.R header says "~92%/8%")
  - Uninsured rests on a single unweighted record, below NAMCS_MIN_RECORDS
    (= 30), so reliable = FALSE (asserted in test-practice-payer-mix.R)
  - shares sum to exactly 1 after dropping the 'Other' tier

Regenerate: Rscript data-raw/namcs/02-namcs_multiyear_acquire.R, then
  namcs_urps_payer_mix() |> readr::write_csv("inst/extdata/namcs_urps_payer_mix.csv")
DUA required: NO (NCHS public-use file)

LOCATION. This file ships in inst/extdata, not in data-raw beside the
acquisition script. data-raw/ is .Rbuildignore'd, so anything under it is
absent from the installed package -- which is exactly what R CMD check runs
its tests against. A vendored fallback placed there is unreachable in the one
environment it exists to serve; it passes under pkgload::load_all() from the
repo root and fails the moment the package is checked properly.
